turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Mr. Darcy's sudden professions of love are as welcome as a thunderstorm on a summer's day, Elizabeth thought, her tone dripping with sarcasm and a hint of disdain.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Mr. Darcy's regard for Elizabeth was genuine, he insisted, and it was astonishing to him that she did not perceive the sincerity of his declaration, given its depth.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Elizabeth's thoughts were a jumble of frustration and distrust, as she pondered Mr. Darcy's sincerity, which seemed as elusive as a mirage on a desert highway. His claims of love only served to remind her of the many affronts he had committed in the past, particularly his treatment of Georgiana, and his cruel words about her own family.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Elizabeth's sensibilities, so prone to misinterpretation, were doubtless clouding her judgment, and preventing her from seeing the sincerity of his own emotions.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Elizabeth's eyes flashed with indignation as she retorted, How dare you suggest that my judgment is clouded, Mr. Darcy, when you have consistently shown such a dearth of understanding and empathy towards others, including herself.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Mr. Darcy's eyes narrowed slightly as he spoke, his tone dripping with a mixture of condescension and annoyance, as he observed that it was quite evident Elizabeth was allowing her prejudices against him to cloud her perception of his character.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Elizabeth's words dripped with disdain, as she wondered how Mr. Darcy could possibly expect her to believe him, given his consistent display of callous disregard for the feelings and well-being of those around him.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Mr. Darcy was appalled, he thought, that Elizabeth could be so obtuse, failing to grasp the depth of his emotions, which were not to be influenced by the faintest hints of scandal or the fleeting judgments of those who barely knew him.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Elizabeth's words dripped with indignation as she asked, how could Mr. Darcy possibly expect her to trust him, when his actions had consistently demonstrated a callous disregard for the feelings of others?

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Elizabeth's lack of discernment is quite remarkable, considering the limited exposure she has had to refined society.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Elizabeth was not to be won over by Mr. Darcy's attempts to charm her into forgetting his haughty reserve and hurtful words, for she saw him clearly, and her perception of him was not to be swayed by empty flattery.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Mr. Darcy was astonished that Elizabeth should so thoroughly misconstrue his character, when the evidence of his good conduct and benevolent intentions was so readily available to be seen.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Elizabeth's eyes flashed with indignation as she pondered the audacity of Mr. Darcy's claim, wondering how he could possibly think that his benevolent intentions would suffice to redeem all the harm he had caused.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Mr. Darcy's eyes narrowed in annoyance as he reflected on the fact that he was being misunderstood by one who should comprehend the true nature of a gentleman, and he could not help but feel that Elizabeth's lack of understanding was a reflection of her own limited experience and education.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Mr. Darcy's professions of love were nothing but a thinly veiled attempt to salvage his wounded pride, for she knew full well that he was incapable of truly loving anyone who did not meet his lofty standards.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: It is a grievous error on Elizabeth's part to suppose that his feelings of love are merely a device to salvage his pride, for he is convinced that his own sentiments are genuine and unfeigned.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: Elizabeth's eyes flashed with indignation as she spoke, her voice laced with a mix of hurt and anger. She was short-sighted, she was not, and she would not be lectured by someone who had never bothered to try to understand her. Mr. Darcy's lack of interest in her as a person was glaring, and now he expected her to swallow his sudden declaration of love whole? The very idea was preposterous.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: Elizabeth's impertinence is truly astonishing, given the liberties she has taken with his character and the affronts she has offered to his family, and yet he finds himself still willing to overlook such transgressions for her sake.

turns.speaker: Elizabeth
turns.text: How ridiculous that he should expect her to believe his professions of love after all the times he had shown her that his pride was far more important to him than any regard for her feelings or well-being.

turns.speaker: Mr. Darcy
turns.text: It is a gross injustice on Elizabeth's part to assume that his affections are merely a ruse, and he dares to hope that she may yet see the sincerity of his declarations.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: Mr. Darcy told Elizabeth that he had struggled in vain, that his feelings would not be repressed, and that he ardently admired and loved her.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Elizabeth replied to Mr. Darcy that it was the established mode to express a sense of obligation for the sentiments avowed, however unequally they may be returned, and that she could not feel gratitude towards him.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: Mr. Darcy remarked to Elizabeth that she had given him no reason to expect a favourable reply, and that he had no great interest in her opinion.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Elizabeth asked Mr. Darcy why he had chosen to tell her that he liked her against his will, against his reason, and even against his character, and whether this was some excuse for incivility.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Elizabeth told Mr. Darcy that she had every reason to think ill of him, and that no motive could excuse the unjust and ungenerous part he had acted in separating her sister from his friend.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Elizabeth asked Mr. Darcy if he could deny that he had been the principal means of dividing her sister from his friend.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: Mr. Darcy told Elizabeth that he had no wish to deny that he had done everything in his power to separate his friend from her sister, and that he rejoiced in his success.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Elizabeth told Mr. Darcy that his character had been unfolded in the recital she received from Mr. Wickham, and that she had never desired his good opinion.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: Mr. Darcy observed to Elizabeth that she took an eager interest in Mr. Wickham's concerns.

opening.speaker: Elizabeth
opening.text: Elizabeth replied to Mr. Darcy that anyone who knew Mr. Wickham's misfortunes could not help feeling an interest in him.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: Mr. Darcy exclaimed to Elizabeth that Mr. Wickham's misfortunes were indeed great.

opening.speaker: Mr. Darcy
opening.text: Mr. Darcy confirmed to Elizabeth that Mr. Wickham's misfortunes had been great indeed.
